caption:
And remember, human beings are biologically wired for connection, co-regulation, love, attachment, community, etc. We are NOT meant to “self-love” ourselves into isolation or stop needing people.

This advice is more for people whose thoughts/ attachment are becoming so consuming that it’s affecting their ability to function, regulate, or feel emotionally safe within themselves day-to-day.
The goal isn’t “don’t need humans or love.”
Quite the opposite actually! The goal is: “I can deeply love/connect with someone without my nervous system collapsing if they pull away!”
Healthy connection is beautiful 🤍 Co-regulation is beautiful 🤍 (and IS coming into your life soon)
Love is beautiful 🤍 and the most powerful thing in this universe!

Emotional dependence that destroys your ability to live/function peacefully is usually a sign there’s deeper nervous system healing needed too. And this method is mainly directed towards helping when healing is needed for day-to-day function :)

try this for 30 days and start noticing the difference 🥹🫶 The thoughts won’t fade
immediately, but eventually you may go a few hours without thinking about them, then a day, then two, then a week — and life gets easier.
The more love = the stronger the effect. Hope
this helps my loves. #manifestation #growth #healing #divinefeminine #focus

title: Retrain Your Brain to Stop Obsessing Over Someone
one_liner: A 30-second morning self-love method to rewire amygdala fear responses around abandonment and obsessive thinking.
key_points: The amygdala flags abandonment as danger (wired in ages 0–6), triggering stress chemicals that force repetitive thoughts about a person
The brain is most neurologically malleable in alpha/theta/delta states — right at waking, falling asleep, or in deep meditation
Method: the moment you wake up, spend 30 seconds speaking to yourself with extreme tenderness (as if to a baby) to retrain the abandonment fear response
After 30 days, obsessive thoughts gradually fade — first hours, then days, then weeks apart
